sources: dossier=Net position 'only the supervisor writes hits' (2026-05-24, artifact) vs. Required behaviors line on TTL housekeeping via reaper tick and resume via control-api (same artifact, self-contradicting the literal 'writes' claim); doc=breakpoint.md:27 'Only the supervisor writes hit rows.'; code=scheduler.go:263 AutoResumeStale (UPDATE) and :270 SweepOrphanedUnresumed (DELETE), controlapi/breakpoints.go Resume path stamps resumed_at (runtime/breakpoint_resume.go), hit CREATE is supervisor-exclusive (breakpoint_eval.go:158)
note: Dossier's own required-behaviors text (resume via control-api, TTL housekeeping via the reaper tick) establishes that non-supervisor roles legitimately mutate existing hit rows; the Net position's 'writes' phrasing is shorthand for hit creation, which code confirms is supervisor-exclusive. Doc corrected to say 'creates' with an explicit carve-out for resume/sweep updates.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'The debug-override channel: ... legal ONLY when the instance is explicitly paused or an unresumed pause-mode hit is blocking a runner' (2026-06-14, bfc9febb, transcript); doc=Purpose paragraph framed the one-shot resume overlay as the sole mutation channel; code=debug_override.go:101-115 HasUnresumedPauseHitForInstance gates set_attribute/invalidate_node, annotated @concept: breakpoint
note: Transcript-tier dossier entry establishes the debug-override channel as a real, distinct consumer of the hit ledger's blocking state, gating persistent mutation separate from the one-shot resume overlay. Doc's Purpose section previously omitted this; added a sentence naming it without duplicating control-api's ownership of the endpoint itself.

sources: dossier=Net position and Required behaviors both name 'L6 resume overlay' twice (2026-05-24, artifact) as the layer applied after the post-L5 bag; doc=breakpoint.md:19,32,33 used 'L6' without defining it; attribute.md:57 defines only L5 (design corpus)
note: Dossier corroborates L6 as real, intentional terminology (the resume-overlay layer applied after concept:attribute's L5 merge), not breakpoint-local jargon or an error. Doc now self-defines L6 at its first substantive use (Boundaries/Owns) so a reader isn't dependent on attribute.md to resolve it. Flagging for the human: attribute.md's merge-stack description still stops at L5 and may warrant a matching cross-reference to L6, but that file is out of this ruling's edit scope.

sources: dossier=silent on breakpoint-infra-failure semantics; no Required-behaviors or Net-position entry addresses it; doc=Invariants section states pause/checkpoint semantics without qualifying failure-mode behavior; code=runner_dispatch.go:452-465 catches BreakpointInfraError, logs 'dispatching with pre-breakpoint bag', returns nil error (pause skipped); runner.go:247-251 and callback.go:491-495 log-and-continue on after_terminal eval errors
note: Question for human: is fail-open on breakpoint-infrastructure error (dispatch proceeds without pausing, hit persistence failures are swallowed) the intended operability posture worth codifying as a doc invariant, or should pause-mode breakpoints instead fail-closed (block dispatch) on infra error so a pause is never silently skipped — matching this codebase's other safety-critical paths (e.g. peer-auth, host-agent), which lean fail-closed? No dossier entry rules on this either way, so code behavior alone cannot establish it as intent.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'The before_dispatch checkpoint fires exactly once per dispatch attempt regardless of how the attribute bag was sourced (sealed/snapshot, schema-less, or full substitution)' (2026-06-21, 10cf843b, transcript); doc=breakpoint.md:35 parenthetical listed 'sealed bag ..., full substitution ..., or a schema-less dispatch with no bag at all' as alternative branches; code=runner_dispatch.go:803-820 loadDispatchBag errors and aborts before the checkpoint when the bag is absent; resolveAttributes:360-407 is one sequential pipeline (sealed bag, then substitution/overrides), not alternative branches
note: The transcript-tier dossier's own three-item list (sealed/snapshot, schema-less, full substitution) does not include a 'no bag at all' case; the doc's added 'with no bag at all' clause misdescribes the schema-less case as bag-less, when code shows a genuinely bag-less run aborts before reaching the checkpoint. Corrected the parenthetical to match the transcript's list and describe the pipeline as sequential rather than branching.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors 'fires exactly once per dispatch attempt' (2026-06-21, 10cf843b, transcript) states no carve-out for executor-less runs; doc=breakpoint.md:35 repeats the transcript's broad claim verbatim; code=runner_dispatch.go:104-113 short-circuits executor-less (pure_cascade/claim_acquired) runs to terminalKindComplete before evaluateBeforeDispatchBreakpoints; runner.go:179 gates resolveAttributes on Executor != ''
note: Question for human: did the transcript's 'fires exactly once per dispatch attempt, regardless of how the bag was sourced' intend to cover executor-less (pure_cascade/claim_acquired) dispatch attempts, which currently never reach the checkpoint at all (fire zero times, not once) — meaning code has a real gap to queue as fix-code — or was the guarantee implicitly scoped to executor-invoking dispatches only (the bag-sourcing framing presupposes a bag is sourced), meaning the doc's unscoped wording should be narrowed instead? The doc's own second sentence already scopes to 'every branch of the dispatcher's attribute-resolution path,' which is narrower than the first sentence's blanket claim — that internal inconsistency is the crux of the ambiguity. Left both sentences as in the transcript/prior doc pending this ruling.

sources: dossier=silent on retry-loop interaction with the checkpoint; doc=breakpoint.md:35 'fires exactly once per dispatch attempt' read as ambiguous about whether each retry re-fires it; code=runner.go:179-181 calls resolveAttributes (containing the checkpoint) once, before the retry loop at runner.go:202-228, which re-invokes dispatch() on IsRetry() without passing back through resolveAttributes
note: Pure wording-clarity fix, not a contested intent question: code is unambiguous that the checkpoint runs once per node-run acquisition, before any retry, and nothing in the dossier or doc disputes that this is the correct behavior. Added an explicit 'not again on any subsequent retry re-invocation of the executor' clause to close the reading that equates 'dispatch attempt' with each executor invocation.

sources: dossier=describes the matcher only at concept altitude ('shared closed 5-key dispatch-identity grammar ... in a shared foundation matcher package', 2026-05-24, artifact) with no function-argument or handler-name detail; design corpus=.ok-planner/CLAUDE.md self-containment rule disallows 'the code at X' pointers and implementation-mechanics prose in concept bodies; doc=Policy-differences section named 'the common foundation matcher package' as an implementation path, 'passing a populated set of used-executor names to the matcher validator' as a function-argument mechanism, and 'the control-api breakpoint matcher-refs check' as a near-symbol name
note: Self-containment is a design-corpus-level house rule for concept docs, independent of the dossier's own casual phrasing. Rewrote the three flagged clauses to state the same behavior at concept altitude (what the validator does, not how it's parametrized or which handler enforces it), removing the rename/move fragility the rule exists to prevent.

sources: dossier=Net position 'Exactly two supervisor checkpoints: before_dispatch ..., after_terminal ...' (2026-05-24, artifact) describes checkpoints as supervisor-wired call sites without assigning doc ownership language either way; doc=breakpoint.md:19 Owns 'the supervisor pre-dispatch and post-terminal checkpoint logic' vs. supervisor.md:19 Owns 'breakpoint checkpoint evaluation at the pre-dispatch and post-terminal checkpoints, blocked-runner polling for resume' — both claim checkpoint evaluation itself
note: Reworded breakpoint.md's Owns/Does-NOT-own split to draw the natural line implied by the doc's own existing ledger-vs-transport reasoning: breakpoint owns matcher evaluation and hit-recording (the decision logic), supervisor owns invoking that logic at the right points in the dispatch flow plus the blocked-runner resume-polling loop (the wiring/mechanics). This narrows breakpoint.md's claim but supervisor.md still independently claims 'breakpoint checkpoint evaluation' verbatim, which now conflicts with breakpoint.md's Does-NOT-own clause; supervisor.md's Owns line likely needs a matching edit (to own only wiring + polling) to fully close the overlap, but that file is out of this ruling's edit scope — flagging for human follow-up.
